 Jeff Hardy ( @jeffhardybrand ) is a professional wrestler with TNA and is known for his time in WWE. He sits down with Chris Van Vliet on the Chris Jericho Cruise to discuss the creative way he was written off TNA TV, whether he thinks a WWE return and Hall of Fame induction is possible, winning the WWE Championship at Armageddon in 2008, his feud with CM Punk, never winning a TLC match in WWE, being part of Macho Man Randy Savage’s final match, an update on his neck injury, and much more!
 Do you ever get tired of hearing that music?
 “No, no, it never gets old. When we returned to WrestleMania in 2017, I said, ‘Yeah, it was cool with that old-ass Hardy Boys music.’ I hated hearing it, but it’s just such a catchy tune. That drumbeat. Anytime you hear that, I know we talked about it a few times before, but I saw that on Ghost Hunters and some other shows. I’m like, well, it’s my music. That’s our music playing on all these different shows. So yes, it never gets old.” 
 How are you feeling? I know you’ve been dealing with some stuff with your neck?
 “I’m feeling alright. It’s just a nagging pain that will not go away. Pretty much before every match, I’m always scared and I freak myself out. I’m going, oh my God, this might be the match that it may become herniated. So dealing with that fear has been kind of rough. But I’m just trying to be safe. I did a pretty crazy Swanton in my last TNA pay-per-view. So actually, it’s kind of hard for me to resist those opportunities because I feel so comfortable and confident when I do those, and we got those foam fingers back now. I was like, if I do this big Swanton, I gotta put those on my hands. Sure enough, I put them on my hands and arms wide open and nailed it.”
 What’s the risk-reward conversation in your head sound like when you’re climbing up a ladder to do a high-risk move like that? 
 “It’s the same thing pretty much every time. I get so excited, and I always say the fear is part of the fun, right? It’s always the same thing. Dear God, dear Lord, great Spirit, please help me survive this and get up from this, and luckily I’ve never missed. The closest I came to missing one was before Matt became Broken Matt Hardy; that Swanton in the Impact Zone. I almost overshot it bad, and I hurt my tailbone pretty good that time too. But that was the closest I came to missing one. So overall, I can’t complain. I’ve been so blessed and I’m so lucky. But that’s my comfort zone. Doing that is what I do best. I really don’t even know how to wrestle.”
 The last time we saw you on TNA you got murdered. So what are we looking at right now? 
 “I’m on the other side. I’m just a hologram. Yeah, in the pro wrestling world, I’m on the other side out there in the stars. It was nasty. But that was one of those things. This Slaughterhouse match idea they came up with, and it was like we had to be real creative to come up with what we were going to do in that match, and it all turned out pretty cool, I thought. Especially when they get done with that, and then you edit it and you watch it back. It’s always so fun, making a little movie. But yeah, that was pretty nasty, man. That’s a hell of a way to take me out. Matt had a really witty name for that thing. He said, ‘This is the real Canadian Destroyer’ because I have issues getting into Canada, and actually, that was a good joke on Matt’s part. It just looked great watching it back, and I just loved it. That was my idea, and so it’s always cool when you dream up something in your imagination, and it comes out so good and so well in reality, and especially in front of a live audience. But yeah, as of right now, storyline-wise, I’m on the other side.”
 Do you think at some point your career will take you back to WWE? Do you think you’ll have another match in WWE? 
 “In a way, I feel like I will. I feel like it’s kind of inevitable that something will happen, whether it be something leading up to the Hall of Fame or whatever, for it to feel right. But yeah, I feel like I have a little more time in a WWE ring before it’s all over.”
 You guys made history; you won the tag team championships in WWE in four consecutive decades: the 90s, the 2000s, the 2010s, and the 2020s. 
 “Very surreal, and it’s almost like I don’t even want to believe it. It’s so crazy. We have been so blessed and lucky to be doing this for so long, and yeah, it’s just crazy cool. We’ve had such a long and successful career, which gives it more meaning and purpose, just to keep on going for as long as we can.”
 What more could you possibly manifest in your professional career? You’ve done absolutely everything. 
 “You are very right. There’s not much. I kind of hate to say this, but I’m such a fan of pro wrestling. I always say Umaga was my favorite feud. But it’s hard not to love the feud between Jeff Hardy and CM Punk. Naturally, when I see him in the WWE universe now, and how good he looks, and how good he’s performing, it’s like, wow, what would that look like? Maybe that’s what I should start manifesting.” 
 What do you think that feud would look like in 2027? CM Punk and Jeff Hardy. 
 “I’m super interested in what the pop would sound like as far as if there’s any chance of me being a little more popular than him at this point, which would be super interesting just to see what would happen. So, yeah, I’m gonna get the manifesting out there.”
 You still get excited at this stage in your career when you think of a new or interesting spot. 
 “I do. I got crazy excited when I thought about a trash can on my head and two axes coming to take me out and put me on the other side in the pro wrestling world. Sure enough, it all worked out so good, but yeah, I still get crazy excited about spots like that. So yeah, I love that stuff.”
 When you talk about taking a little bit of time off, how much of that is to dive into the music and get that out there? How much of it is also to give your neck a bit of a break from taking bumps? 
 “ It’s mainly for the neck , like I said earlier, before every match, I’m freaking out like I’m gonna make the bulging disc herniated.” 
 Are you hurting right now? 
 “No, it’s not terrible. When I paint for a while and my head’s down for a long time, I can really feel it, and sleep has kind of not been that great because it does bug me at night. So it’s not a terrible pain, but I don’t want it to be a terrible pain. That’s what I’m afraid of, naturally. But yeah, I just feel like I need a break from pro wrestling just for a few months.”
 Was there ever talk of having Willow in WWE? 
 “No, no, never at all. TNA was the first that they allowed Willow to become a thing, and I do have a brand new Willow mask, man. It’s super cool. I definitely want to bring it to life. It’s going to take a lot to get ready, but it’s the new faceplate, and it looks very different from the original Willow mask. But Willow’s got such a good look. I think this new look is going to be better than the older look, and give it a new, modern feel, and be super special.” 
 Do you think you understand Jeff Hardy?
 “From time to time, I do. Yeah, I do. But I think now, as I’m getting older, I think I’m starting to understand more than ever. Especially, I think kids have a lot to do with that when you become a parent.”
 I saw a crazy stat the other day that Jeff Hardy has never won a TLC match. Can you believe that? You have won a Full Metal Mayhem. But in WWE Jeff Hardy’s never won a TLC match. 
 “If you asked me that, I’d have thought I won one. Isn’t that crazy? Yeah, that is stupid crazy. You’re right. I have no idea. You know, Taker had the undefeated streak, but I never won a match at WrestleMania for the longest time. I don’t know. I did win in 2017. I think that was my first.” 
 2008 was such a special year for you. It’s the year you won the WWE Championship at Armageddon in December of that year. At what point did you start to feel the momentum behind you that you were, at that time, the most popular wrestler on the planet? 
 “Yeah, and I gotta give props. I think Freddie Prinze Jr., he was on the creative team. He had a lot to do with me becoming the World Champion. So I’m forever grateful for him vouching for me and believing in me. So yeah, it was just one of those things, man. It’s like, oh my God, this is crazy. I’m about to achieve a childhood dream that so many people dream of and never, never reach. When you reach for the brass ring and finally get it, it was just a childhood dream that came true and all that hard work leading up to everything we’ve done in WWE just made it all so special.”
 Can you put into words what you were feeling after that 1, 2, 3 at Armageddon in 2008 when you became the WWE Champion? 
 “Yeah, I don’t know, man. It was just, gosh, you could just tell in the celebration. It was just so much hard work and so many years of just believing in myself and in Matt, and just knowing that it could happen if I would put in the work and just work as hard as I possibly could and do whatever I could to make people remember who Jeff Hardy is after they see a Jeff Hardy match. So yeah, it was just again a childhood dream that came true. I think the coolest thing about it was bringing the title to my dad. Because naturally my dad became our biggest fan because he never understood why I would save up from my landscaping job to buy a ladder and then that ladder was destroyed. ‘Jeffrey, what are you doing buying these ladders and destroying them? This don’t make any sense. You’re never gonna do anything in this pro wrestling.’ No, it’s gonna be fine. So he became our biggest fan after and he finally understood after he started seeing the TLC matches as to why I would do that. I’m so grateful for the object known as the ladder. I’m so grateful.”
 I don’t know if you’ve talked about this, but you were part of Randy Savage’s last match ever. So it’s Randy Savage, AJ Styles, and Jeff Hardy versus Kevin Nash, Scott Hall, and Jeff Jarrett in TNA. What a legendary match! What do you remember from that day?
 “I just remember marking out like crazy, meeting Randy Savage for the first time. I’d never met him before that. Yeah, I’d never met him until that. It was just so crazy. I was about to put together a match with the Macho Man Randy Savage, and it was crazy. Speaking of that match, there’s an action figure. They made some action figures back in that time with the white pants on, and I just painted my whole chest and my neck. I want to bring that look back at a TNA pay-per-view or something because it was a cool look. The action figure, and being that it was the Macho Man’s last match, I had no idea that that was his last match. Wow, that’s crazy cool that I was in the Macho Man’s last match.” 
 Did you have a moment in the ring where you’re like, my God, that’s the Macho Man? 
 “I had several moments, and what I remember most about that was something with a sunset flip, and they asked him if he could do something. I don’t know if it’s Hall or Nash or Jeff, they asked him if he could do something. He said, ‘Oh no, I can’t do that, brother. My knees might go flying into the front row.’ He said something crazy that he couldn’t do that because his knees were bad or something, but gosh, that’s crazy.”
 What is Jeff Hardy grateful for?
 “My wife and daughters, my dogs, and pro wrestling.”
